statement.p: (a) If \sum_{i=1}^3 x_i = 4, find the values of x_1, x_2, x_3 making \sum_{i=1}^3 {x_i}^2 minimum.

p.em: (Give your values as a comma separated list.)

statement.p: (b) Generalize the result of part (a) to find the minimum value of \sum_{i=1}^n{x_i}^2 subject to \sum_{i=1}^n x_i=4.

static.solution:
(a) Let f(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sum_{i=1}^3{x_i}^2 = {x_1}^2 + {x_2}^2 + {x_3}^2 and g(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sum_{i=1}^3 x_i = 4. Then \nabla f = \lambda\nabla g gives 2x_1 = \lambda = 2x_2 = 2x_3. so x_1 = x_2 = x_3 = \frac{\lambda}2. Then x_1+x_2+x_3 = 4 gives 3\frac{\lambda}{2} = 4\quad\hbox{ so } \quad \lambda = \frac{8}{3}. Thus x_1 = x_2 = x_3 = \frac{4}{3}.
These values of x_1, x_2,x_3 give the minimum (rather than maximum) because the value of without bound as x_2,x_2,x_3\to\infty.
(b) A similar argument shows that \sum_{i=1}^nx_i has its minimum value subject to \sum_{i=1}^nx_i = 4 when x_1=x_2=\cdots= x_n=\frac{4}n. Then the minimum value is \sum_1^n \left(\frac{4}{n}\right)^2 = n\cdot \left(\frac{4}{n}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{n}.
